Burnt Oak Primary School
Apply now
Welcome to Burnt Oak Primary School
It is a real privilege to be the Headteacher of Burnt Oak Primary School, a school full of wonderful children, dedicated staff and a strong sense of community.
With over 20 years of experience in education, my passion has never changed: to ensure that every child feels valued, is inspired to achieve and has the opportunity to flourish.
At Burnt Oak, we believe that primary education should be about so much more than academic achievement. It should be a journey filled with discovery, excitement, challenge and memorable experiences that shape the people our children become.
Our school mission captures this ambition:
“We all flourish from a wealth of learning experiences that positively impact on academic, physical and emotional success.”
This is not simply a statement; it is a commitment that guides everything we do. We have high expectations for every child, providing an ambitious and engaging curriculum alongside enriching opportunities that develop confidence, independence, resilience and a lifelong love of learning.
At the heart of our school is The Burnt Oak Way, built upon our four character values: Empathy, Responsibility, Resilience and Respect. These values shape our relationships, our choices and the positive, nurturing environment in which our children grow.
I firmly believe that the very best education happens when children, families and staff work together. Through this partnership, we are building a school where children feel safe, happy and proud to belong, where individuality is celebrated and where every success, however big or small, matters.
Our ambition is simple: for every child to leave Burnt Oak not only well prepared for the next stage of their education, but with the confidence, character and aspirations to embrace the opportunities that lie ahead.
I warmly invite you to explore our website and discover what makes Burnt Oak such a special place to learn and grow.
Matt WignellHeadteacher

Burnt Oak Primary School
British Values at Burnt Oak
At Burnt Oak Primary School, we want every child to grow into a confident, respectful and responsible member of their community.
We actively promote the fundamental British values of:
Democracy • The Rule of Law • Individual Liberty • Mutual Respect • Tolerance of Different Faiths and Beliefs
These values are not taught as a one-off topic. They are woven throughout our curriculum, assemblies, relationships, behaviour expectations and everyday school life.
They work hand in hand with The Burnt Oak Way and our Character Values of Empathy, Respect, Resilience and Responsibility, helping our children understand themselves, understand others and make a positive contribution to the world around them.
🗳️ Democracy
We teach children that their voice matters and that they can contribute to decisions that affect them.
Children learn about democracy through the curriculum and experience it in action through opportunities to express their views, vote, represent others and contribute to school life.
We encourage children to listen carefully to different opinions, discuss ideas respectfully and understand that decisions will not always reflect their own personal choice.
⚖️ The Rule of Law
Children learn why rules and laws are important in keeping people safe, protecting individual rights and helping communities to live and work together.
Our school rules and expectations provide children with a practical understanding of rights, responsibilities and consequences.
Through The Burnt Oak Way, children learn to take responsibility for their choices, understand how their behaviour affects others and recognise the importance of fairness.
🕊️ Individual Liberty
We want our children to become increasingly confident and independent, making informed choices within a safe and supportive environment.
Children are encouraged to express themselves, develop their own interests and opinions and understand that everyone has rights and freedoms.
Alongside these freedoms, we teach children that our choices carry responsibilities and that the rights and freedoms of others must also be respected.
🤝 Mutual Respect
Respect is at the heart of The Burnt Oak Way.
Children learn that everyone deserves to be treated with dignity, kindness and respect, regardless of their background, identity, beliefs or circumstances.
Our curriculum provides opportunities for children to encounter different experiences and perspectives, challenge stereotypes and develop empathy for others.
Discrimination, prejudice and derogatory behaviour have no place at Burnt Oak.
🌍 Tolerance of Different Faiths and Beliefs
We celebrate the fact that Britain is a diverse society.
Through our curriculum, particularly RE, PSHE, assemblies and wider experiences, children learn about a range of faiths, beliefs, cultures and ways of life, including those of people who do not hold a religious belief.
We encourage children to be curious, ask respectful questions and understand that people can hold beliefs and opinions that are different from their own.
Children learn that difference is something to understand and respect, not fear.
British Values Across Our Curriculum
British Values can be seen throughout school life, including through:
Our approach is age appropriate and helps children learn not simply what these values are, but why they matter and how they can demonstrate them in their everyday lives.
PSHE and Relationships Education
Religious Education
assemblies and character education
discussions, debates and opportunities to respectfully disagree
online safety and responsible digital citizenship
Preparing Children for Life in Modern Britain
Ultimately, promoting British Values is about preparing our children for the world beyond Burnt Oak.
We want our children to leave us able to think for themselves, listen to others, challenge discrimination, respect difference, understand their rights and responsibilities and participate positively in their communities.
Together with our Character Values of Empathy, Respect, Resilience and Responsibility, British Values help us fulfil our mission:
We all flourish from a wealth of learning experiences that positively impact on academic, physical and emotional success.

Burnt Oak Primary School
Values and Ethos
At Burnt Oak Primary School, everything we do is guided by our commitment to helping every child achieve Academic, Physical and Emotional Success.
These three areas sit at the heart of our school ethos and reflect our belief that education is about developing the whole child. Our curriculum, wider opportunities, relationships and decisions are all shaped by our mission:
“We all flourish from a wealth of learning experiences that positively impact on academic, physical and emotional success.”
We recognise that success will look different for every child. Our role is to understand each child's starting point, provide the right opportunities and support, and enable every child to flourish and achieve their potential.
Academic Success
Academic success gives our children the knowledge, skills and confidence they need to thrive in an increasingly complex and changing world.
We want children to become curious, motivated and independent learners who take pride in their achievements and understand that success comes through effort, perseverance and a willingness to learn.
We recognise that academic success looks different for every child. By understanding individual starting points and providing an ambitious, inclusive curriculum, we aim to ensure that every child makes excellent progress.
We celebrate achievement in all its forms, including the small steps that can represent significant success for an individual child. Through this, we aim to develop intrinsic motivation, encouraging children to want to learn, improve and achieve because they value learning itself.
Physical Success
Physical success is about helping children develop the knowledge, habits and confidence to lead healthy, active lives.
Being physically active supports children's health and wellbeing and can positively influence concentration, memory and readiness to learn. It also provides opportunities for children to develop teamwork, resilience, confidence and an understanding of how their choices can contribute to a healthy lifestyle.
We promote physical success through:
high-quality PE lessons
links with secondary school PE provision
sports clubs and additional sporting opportunities
Sports Leaders at breaktimes
active play and lunchtimes
Emotional Success
Emotional success is fundamental to children's wellbeing, relationships and ability to flourish.
We want our children to develop a strong understanding of themselves and others. By developing self-awareness, emotional literacy and positive relationships, children are better equipped to communicate effectively, solve problems, manage challenges and form relationships based on trust and mutual respect.
Developing empathy also enables children to understand different perspectives, recognise the feelings and experiences of others and contribute positively to their community.
We promote emotional success through:
a well-established RSHE curriculum
developing positive, independent and collaborative relationships
celebrating and appreciating diversity
maintaining high expectations for behaviour and manners
The Burnt Oak Way
Alongside our commitment to Academic, Physical and Emotional Success, we explicitly teach the character children need to flourish.
In an ever-changing world, knowledge alone is not enough. We want our children to develop positive characteristics that will support them throughout their education and into adult life.
Our four Character Values form The Burnt Oak Way:
💚 Empathy
We want our children to understand and care about the experiences and feelings of others.
We teach children to look beyond simply tolerating difference. We want them to value diversity, challenge discrimination and stand alongside others when something is unfair or wrong.
💛 Responsibility
We want our children to become active, independent and responsible learners who take pride in themselves, their work, their school and their community.
Children learn to understand that their choices have consequences and that each of us has a responsibility for the way we behave, learn and treat others.
💙 Resilience
We want our children to develop the confidence and determination to face challenges, learn from setbacks and keep going when things are difficult.
We teach children that mistakes are part of learning and encourage them to approach challenges positively, seek support when they need it and strive to become the best version of themselves.
❤️ Respect
We want our children to value themselves, others and the world around them, demonstrating kindness, understanding and consideration in everything they do.
Children learn that respect extends to people whose experiences, backgrounds, beliefs or opinions may be different from their own.
Helping Every Child to Flourish
Together, our three areas of success and four Character Values define what we want for every child at Burnt Oak.
Academic, Physical and Emotional Success describe what we want our children to achieve.
Empathy, Responsibility, Resilience and Respect describe the character we want them to develop along the way.
Together, they create The Burnt Oak Way and help prepare our children to flourish at school, in their communities and in the wider world.
Progression in Character Values
Our character values help pupils develop resilience, confidence, independence, and respect for others (personal development). It includes fostering responsible citizenship, promoting mental health and wellbeing, and ensuring pupils understand and live by fundamental British values:

PE and School Sport
At Burnt Oak Primary School, we are committed to providing an outstanding PE curriculum that enables every child to develop the knowledge, skills, and confidence to lead active, healthy lives both now and in the future. We have chosen the Rising Stars Champions PE scheme as the foundation of our PE provision because it aligns closely with our school values and educational priorities. The Rising Stars Champions scheme provides a comprehensive framework that covers all National Curriculum requirements for PE at Key Stages 1 and 2, including core subjects such as games, gymnastics, dance, athletics, outdoor and adventurous activities, and swimming. This ensures that our pupils receive their full entitlement to a broad and balanced PE curriculum. The scheme provides:
Assessment frameworks: Built-in assessment tools help teachers track pupil progress and identify where additional support may be needed

Burnt Oak Primary School
Maths
We use maths in every aspect of our lives at work and in practical everyday activities at home and beyond. Being numerate is an essential life skill that fosters analytical reasoning skills which are important for solving problems and looking for solutions.
Having good mathematical skills can also develop resilience and perseverance providing ways of developing strong mental discipline which is good for mental health. Maths encourages logical reasoning, critical and creative thinking, abstract thinking and can help improve communication skills.
To make the best choices, we need to be numerate

Burnt Oak Primary School
PSHE
Burnt Oak adopts the Jigsaw PSHE scheme throughout the school from Nursery to Year 6. Jigsaw is taught progressively throughout the school and is at the heart of our curriculum to prepare our children to achieve emotional success (one of our values) alongside physical and academic success. The age-appropriate lessons support the spiritual, moral, social, cultural, mental and physical development of pupils, at school and in society. Safeguarding underpins every lesson in Jigsaw and supports our complete commitment to safeguarding our pupils. The concepts taught throughout Jigsaw are: empathy, identity and safety.
British Values and SMSC are mapped throughout Jigsaw. The Department for Education (DfE) has stated: “Personal, social, health and economic (PSHE) education is an important and necessary part of all pupils’ education. All schools should teach PSHE, drawing on good practice, and this expectation is outlined in the introduction to the proposed new national curriculum.” The PSHE Association states “PSHE education gives pupils the knowledge, skills, and attributes they need to keep themselves healthy and safe and to prepare them for life and work in modern Britain…. When taught well, PSHE education helps pupils to achieve their academic potential, and leave school equipped with skills they will need throughout later life.”
Jigsaw holds children at its heart, and its cohesive vision helps children understand and value how they fit into and contribute to the world. With strong emphasis on emotional literacy, building resilience and nurturing mental and physical health, Jigsaw 3-11 properly equips schools to deliver engaging and relevant PSHE within a whole-school approach. Jigsaw lessons also include mindfulness allowing children to advance their emotional awareness, concentration and focus.
To ensure a depth and accuracy of learning which builds upon prior learning, all classes undertake weekly PSHE lessons which follow Jigsaw 3-11, a fully planned and spiralling/progressive PSHE scheme. As a school, we follow a set theme each half term, which is introduced, in a whole school assembly. Lessons are underpinned by the Jigsaw behaviour charter, which reinforces our character values of empathy and responsibility.
The 6 Jigsaw themes are:
Being Me in My World
Celebrating Difference (including Anti-Bullying)
Relationships (including Relationships and Sex Education)
In addition, Anti-bullying week, Internet Safety Day, charity days, road safety, restart a heart sessions and support from our pastoral and SEN team enhance the mission of our PSHE curriculum.
Assessment: The teacher records sessions in their online class Jigsaw book & assess each child termly via RAG rating.
Each Jigsaw puzzle complements and promotes our character values.
Relationships and Sex Education:
At Burnt Oak Primary our RSE curriculum is firmly embedded in our Jigsaw (PSHE) curriculum. An important part of the Jigsaw PSHE programme is delivered through the 'Relationships' and 'Changing Me' puzzle pieces which are covered in the summer term.
There are four main aims of teaching RSE:
Each year group will be taught appropriate to their age and developmental stage. At no point will a child be taught something that is inappropriate.
Below is a summary of RSE coverage within the Jigsaw scheme for each year group:
Jigsaw, the mindful approach to PSHE, is a progressive and spiral scheme of learning. In planning the lessons, Jigsaw PSHE ensures that learning from previous years is revisited and extended, adding new concepts, knowledge and skills, year on year as appropriate. The table below draws out the spiral knowledge and skills progression within all six Puzzles (units of work) including the key vocabulary used in each year group; explicit links to the DfE statutory Relationships and Health Education outcomes have been made in each Puzzle.
INTENT: Jigsaw holds children at its heart, and its cohesive vision helps children understand and value how they fit into and contribute to the world. With strong emphasis on emotional literacy, building resilience and nurturing mental and physical health, Jigsaw 3-11 properly equips schools to deliver engaging and relevant PSHE within a whole-school approach. Jigsaw lessons also include mindfulness allowing children to advance their emotional awareness, concentration, focus and self-regulation.
IMPLEMENTATION: Jigsaw 3-11 offers a comprehensive programme for Primary PSHE, including statutory Relationships and Health Education, in a spiral, progressive and fully planned scheme of work, giving children relevant learning experiences to help them navigate their world and to develop positive relationships with themselves and others.
IMPACT: This can be established through assessment identified in the key learning.
Burnt Oak Primary School

Burnt Oak Primary School
RE
We follow the Jigsaw RE scheme of work throughout the school from FS1 to Year 6. It is taught progressively throughout the school, enabling children to learn about a range of religions throughout their school life. Whilst we learn a lot about religious beliefs, we also consider how religious values are not so different to our own values; exploring links that we can make between our own lives and those of people who follow a religion. This underpins the concept of community which is taught throughout our RE curriculum.
Jigsaw RE says that, “We believe RE is a vitally important component of children’s personal, social and spiritual development. Developing an understanding of their own and others’ worldviews underpins the growth of empathy and respect. Appreciating that we all see the world through the lens that has been formed by our experiences, upbringing, culture etc and that this influences our decision-making and our own way of seeing the world is so valuable.”
Christianity is taught for three terms in each year group from FS1 – Year 6, showing clear progression. Other religions covered include Judaism (years 1 and 4), Islam (years 2 and 6), Sanatana Dharma (year 3) and Sikhism (year 5). After Christianity, these are the most celebrated religions in our local demographic and are taught for the remaining three terms per year. Jigsaw RE gives a comprehensive structure for RE across the whole primary school, provides a key enquiry question for each half-term, selects the most appropriate subject knowledge to be taught to enable children to answer the enquiry question and goes on to provide assessment tasks, resources and attainment descriptors, with exemplification.
Burnt Oak Primary School

Burnt Oak Primary School
Reading
Why Reading is Important at Burnt Oak Primary School
Reading is at the centre of our curriculum at Burnt Oak Primary School. It's the foundation for lifelong learning and opens doors to endless opportunities for our children. We place reading at the centre of everything we do because we recognise that strong reading skills unlock access to learning across all subjects. By prioritising reading we aim to support all our pupils in accessing all areas of the curriculum and developing the communication skills they need for future success
Reading at the Heart of Our Curriculum
Pupils are regularly immersed in high-quality children's literature ensuring that reading permeates every aspect of school life. This approach means that whether children are learning about history, science, or any other subject, reading provides the gateway to knowledge and understanding. Books transport children to different worlds, times, and situations, sparking creativity and helping them envision possibilities beyond their immediate experience.
Building Strong Foundations Through Phonics
We use Read Write Inc Phonics to give every child a systematic and structured approach to learning to read and spell. Read Write Inc Phonics is a structured and consistent approach to the learning of phonics that helps pupils develop their reading fluency and spelling. The Key Leaders It's a DfE-validated systematic synthetic phonics programme designed to give children the best possible start in reading and writing.
Phonics is taught daily in the Early Years Foundation Stage (EYFS) and KS1, to groups set by ability. This ensures every child receives teaching matched to their current phonics knowledge and skills. Grouping and assessment:
Children are grouped by their phonics ability, not their age or class
Pupils are assessed every half term, which supports rapid progress
Groups are flexible, allowing children to move up as soon as they're ready
Each lesson typically includes:
Speed Sounds – learning new sounds and practising those already taught
Read the word – blending sounds to read words
Read the story – applying phonics skills to read books matched to their level
Spelling – using phonics knowledge to spell words
Writing – composing sentences using the sounds and words learned
Pupils who still need to learn phonics, will continue to be taught in KS2 as well. This consistent approach ensures that all children develop the decoding skills they need to become confident, fluent readers.
Reading books at home
Children bring home Read Write Inc books that are carefully matched to their phonics level. This means they can practise the sounds they've learned in school and build confidence as successful readers. Children also have access to online Read Write Inc books and quizzes through Oxford Owls
Developing Fluency After Phonics
After completing the phonics-based Read Write Inc program, we use Book Bands (Gold, White and Lime) to continue to develop fluency and confidence for independent and home reading. Books are matched to pupils' reading ability and ensure that books challenge pupils appropriately while maintaining their confidence. Pupils are listened to on a one-to-one in class and running records are used to assess progress and when pupils are ready to move up to the next level. It is expected that pupils are reading White books at the end of year 2 and Lime books in year 3. After Lime we then use Accelerated Reader assessments to give them a level book that can be chosen from our library or class book corners. This is alongside a whole class reading approach which is introduced from year 2 onwards, at the point where pupils' decoding skills are secure. This transition is crucial for moving pupils from phonics-based reading to more advanced comprehension and fluency work. This approach helps our pupils transition smoothly from Read Write Inc to becoming confident, fluent readers who can comprehend and engage with challenging texts.
Developing Comprehension and Love of Reading
A carefully curated collection of high-quality texts forms the backbone of our English and Reading curriculum, ensuring all pupils experience a diverse range of literature throughout their time at school to challenge and inspire them.
Beyond phonics, our English curriculum and reading lessons focus on developing reading fluency, deep comprehension skills and vocabulary. Reading fluency – the ability to read accurately, at an appropriate pace, and with expression – is essential for pupils to access the curriculum and develop as confident readers.
We use an 'I do, we do, you do' teaching approach to build confidence and independence:
I do: The teacher models fluent reading, demonstrating intonation, expression, pacing and comprehension strategies. This shows children what good reading sounds like and helps them understand how to bring texts to life
We do: The class works together, with the teacher guiding pupils through high-level questioning and discussion as they explore challenging texts. We use echo reading as a key strategy to develop fluency – the teacher models fluent reading of a short segment and pupils repeat the segment, copying the teacher's expression, pace and intonation. This technique helps pupils develop confidence and improves their reading fluency in a supportive environment
You do: Pupils apply their skills independently, reading with confidence, fluency and understanding
These lessons include a range of activities that enable pupils to develop their vocabulary and comprehension skills.
Supporting Every Reader
We use Read Write Inc, Accelerated Reader and PiXL assessments to track progress and ensure every child receives the support they need. These tools help us identify where children need additional help and celebrate their achievements as they progress. We are developing a new reading support programme – BRP (Building reading Power) for those pupils who need additional support on their reading journey.
Reading For Pleasure
Our school library is the heart of reading at Burnt Oak. It is a welcoming reading environment where children can explore and books independently, listen to stories and engage in book talk. We know that children who read for enjoyment are more likely to succeed academically and develop into confident, curious learners.
Teachers read to their class everyday which is a vital opportunity for teachers to model fluent, expressive reading to pupils, building their love of stories and developing comprehension skills through shared reading experiences.
We encourage children to share books and read regularly at home. Our Reading Bear to reward this is an initiative that provides recognition and motivation for pupils' reading achievements, creating excitement around reading progress and making reading feel special and rewarding. We also offer tangible rewards that celebrate reading achievements and encourage continued engagement with books. We also have other reading challenges, linked with celebration of reading such as World Book Day, to motivate and celebrate reading.
Developing Character Values
Reading plays a crucial role in developing our school character values of empathy, responsibility, respect, and resilience, whilst also nurturing imagination:
Empathy: Through stories, children experience different perspectives, cultures, and emotions, helping them understand and relate to others' feelings and experiences
Responsibility: Regular reading habits teach children to take ownership of their learning and develop self-discipline in completing reading tasks
Respect: Exposure to diverse characters and viewpoints through literature helps children appreciate differences and develop respect for others
Resilience: Encountering challenges faced by characters in books helps children understand how to persevere through difficulties and develop problem-solving skills
Creating Lifelong Learners
Ultimately, reading is about more than passing tests - it’s about equipping our children with the skills and love of learning they'll carry throughout their lives. Our aim is to provide the necessary lifelong skills to become avid readers.
When children read widely and often, they develop vocabulary, critical thinking skills, cultural awareness, and the ability to express themselves confidently – all essential for success in every subject and every aspect of life. At Burnt Oak Primary School, we're committed to ensuring every child becomes a confident, enthusiastic reader who sees books as a gateway to understanding the world and developing into well-rounded individuals with strong values and boundless imagination.
Early Years Foundation Stage
By the end of Reception, children should be well prepared to reach a good level of development, securing important foundational knowledge in literacy, which paves the way for future learning in Year 1 and beyond.
Word Reading Early Learning Goal
Comprehension Early Learning Goal
Children at the expected level of development will:
Say a sound for each letter in the alphabet and at least 10 digraphs
Read words consistent with their phonic knowledge by sound-blending
Read aloud simple sentences and books that are consistent with their phonic knowledge, including some common exception words
Children at the expected level of development will:
Demonstrate understanding of what has been read to them by retelling stories and narratives using their own words and recently introduced vocabulary
Anticipate (where appropriate) key events in stories
Use and understand recently introduced vocabulary during discussions about stories, non-fiction, rhymes and poems and during role play
Burnt Oak Reading Spine
Our reading spine provides a carefully curated selection of texts organised by year group (from Nursery through to Year 6) and across different terms throughout the academic year. This structure serves several key educational purposes:
Ensuring Curriculum Coverage and Progression
The spine ensures all pupils experience a broad range of high-quality literature as they progress through school. By mapping specific texts to each year group and term, we guarantee that children encounter increasingly complex texts that build on their prior reading experiences.
Creating a Shared Reading Culture
When all children in a year group read the same core texts, it creates common reference points for discussion, builds a shared literary heritage within our school community, and enables teachers to plan collaborative activities around these texts.
Supporting Planning and Assessment
Teachers can plan their English curriculum with confidence, knowing which texts will be taught when. This allows for:
Exposing Children to Diverse Literature
Our spine includes a rich variety of authors, illustrators, genres and themes - from classic tales to contemporary stories, poetry collections, and texts representing diverse voices and experiences. This breadth ensures children encounter different writing styles, perspectives and cultural contexts.
Building Reading Stamina and Enjoyment
The spine includes different categories - core English texts, class reads, and RFP (Reading for Pleasure) texts - which together support children's development as confident, enthusiastic readers who read both for learning and for enjoyment.
Our reading spine is a cornerstone of how we deliver our mission: "We all flourish from a wealth of learning experiences that positively impact on academic, physical and emotional success."
Every child, from Nursery to Year 6, has access to the same high-quality literary experiences, ensuring equity and opportunity for all learners. The diverse range of texts, authors, genres and themes provide rich, varied experiences that go far beyond a single textbook approach. Carefully sequenced texts build reading skills, vocabulary, comprehension and writing models that drive academic progress. Texts such as 'Sportopedia' (Year 2), books about Mo Farah and Usain Bolt, and stories celebrating physical achievement inspire children to value movement and wellbeing. It also includes books exploring feelings, relationships, challenges and triumphs help children develop emotional literacy and resilience.
Developing Character Values Through Literature
Our reading spine is also a powerful vehicle for developing the key character values that underpin our school ethos: empathy, respect, resilience, and responsibility.
The carefully selected texts allow children to step into different characters' shoes and experience life from diverse perspectives. For example:
Through these stories, children learn to understand others' feelings, motivations and experiences - developing the empathy needed to be kind and considerate members of your school community.
Many texts in our spine celebrate diversity and challenge stereotypes, teaching children to value difference and treat everyone with dignity:
These books provide natural opportunities to discuss respect for others, for our environment, and for different viewpoints.
Our spine features numerous characters who face challenges, overcome obstacles and demonstrate determination:
These stories help children understand that setbacks are part of learning and that persistence leads to success.
Many texts explore themes of taking responsibility for our actions, our community and our world:
These books provide springboards for discussions about personal responsibility, caring for others, and being active citizens.
Better preparation and resource gathering
Consistent assessment opportunities across classes
More effective moderation between teachers
'All Are Welcome' (Nursery/Reception) promotes inclusivity
'Mixed' (Reception/Year 2) explores identity and acceptance
'Tidy' (Year 2) explores environmental responsibility

Burnt Oak Primary School

Burnt Oak Primary School
Writing
Our writing curriculum is designed to provide a broad and balanced education that meets the needs of all children. We follow the award-winning Ready Steady Write from Literacy Counts to develop confident, independent and successful writers with high aspirations. Our writing curriculum is research-informed and impact-proven, carefully designed to support all children to master the foundational skills and write for a clear audience and purpose. Through the use of high-quality, vocabulary-rich texts, we provide exciting and meaningful reasons to write. Children are immersed in literature and taught to craft their writing with precision, using a range of pedagogical approaches, including sentence accuracy, modelled writing and shared writing, as well as regular opportunities for editing. We value spoken language as a foundation for writing. Through structured talk, drama and vocabulary exploration, children learn how to organise and express their ideas clearly before writing them down. Our aim is for every child – regardless of need – to write fluently and take pride in their work. We want our pupils to leave primary school as enthusiastic writers, ready for the next stage of their education.
Implementation:
Organisation and Curriculum Coverage: Ready Steady Write empowers teachers to provide high-quality teaching of writing through high-quality literature. These detailed units of work centre on engaging, vocabulary-rich texts, with a wealth of writing opportunities within and across the curriculum. They provide:
Our English curriculum is developed around a sequence of high-quality age-appropriate texts, using Literacy Count’s Ready Steady Write units of learning. We use each book to create opportunities to:
Building on this foundation, we teach literacy using a range of strategies which include:
Class teachers ensure that the Writing process is clearly evident on working walls, with modelled examples being available to all pupils as the sequence of lessons develops.
Resources: each class has a resource box with their Ready Steady Write vehicle texts, reveal objects and supplementary texts which support the themes and genre being taught for that half term. The lesson plans, resources and leadership support is found on the membership homepage online. The Enhancements for the units can be seen in our indoor and outdoor areas in EYFS.
Working Walls and Table Resources: each class is expected to develop an English working wall which adapts daily with teaching. Displays should model the writing process and scaffolds needed for children to apply to their own writing. Spellings, handwriting and supporting phonics materials should also be displayed within the classroom to aid children’s writing. Sentence accuracy checkers are available to all children, both in their books and in the environment. Staff will model the expectations throughout the curriculum.
Planning: the entire writing curriculum is mapped out on coverage and progression documents. Then, the Ready Steady Write units include all of the resources needed for each teacher to plan and deliver lessons. There are a range of scaffolds and supporting resources and teachers tweak and shape the units to meet the specific needs of their children. There are also assessment proformas which are completed half termly and identify next steps for children.
Clear sequential Episodes of Learning
Wider reading for the wider curriculum
Example Texts linked to writing outcomes
A wealth of supporting resource
Inclusion:
Children with English as an additional language:
It is vital that children who have English as an additional language have English modelled accurately by all staff at school. Collaborative work with peers (where English is their first language) is essential and EAL children should be provided with consistent opportunities for this verbal interaction. All teachers include a range of strategies to support children with EAL which includes:
Teachers work with the SENDCO to best meet the needs of individuals within their classes. Children who are new to English are assessed and support is put in place by the SENDCO to help them make rapid progress.
Children with Special Educational Needs:
Some children experience learning difficulties, which affect their progress in English. Class teachers inform the SENDCO if they are concerned that a child may have underlying learning difficulties. Some children then receive SEN support. This may include:
Confident and competent writers: children are given opportunities to deepen their knowledge in writing and to effectively draw upon their reading when constructing texts. writing groups and differentiation. Lesson plans for Ready Steady Write include appropriate challenge and these are considered when delivering lessons.
Repetition and recasting of language features
Impact
The innovative practice across the school provides a strong foundation and opportunities for children to collaborate and develop social skills both indoors and out. This curriculum design ensures that the needs of individual and small groups of children can be met within the environment of quality first teaching, supported by targeted, proven interventions where appropriate. In this way it can be seen to impact in a very positive way on children’s outcomes. High quality visits and visitors to the school enhance the curriculum and provide opportunities for Writing for a purpose. Children have opportunities to share their learning with each other, their parents and carers and other learners through school-based and external exhibitions, performances, competitions and events involving other schools. Developing their independence and motivation as learners and their sense of responsibility as future citizens is at the heart of all our teaching and learning. As a result, we have a community of enthusiastic writers who enjoy showcasing their developing literacy knowledge and skills. They are confident to take risks in their writing, and love to discuss and share their ideas.
Teachers draw upon observations and continuous assessment to ensure children are stretched and challenged and to identify those children who may need additional support. Formative assessment of Writing is completed through teachers’ daily feedback to inform future planning. Teachers use the children’s everyday writing and adapt models and input to meet their current needs. Teachers also complete a Reflecting on Unit outcomes document after each half termly unit, to identify next steps and the subsequent units are amended to include these focuses. Daily sentence accuracy work is carefully monitored to ensure children are constructing sentences both coherently and accurately. Termly staff meetings allow for whole school moderation of writing to deepen understanding of standards.
Subject leaders will analyse 3 X termly data and address areas for curriculum development. Children’s attainment, progress and barriers to learning will be discussed in Pupil Progress Meetings with senior leaders and clear actions to work on will be planned together, to support pupils and staff in closing gaps.
Expectations for the classroom environment:
Handwriting Progression Plan
In Reception, we concentrate on building both gross and fine motor skills needed for handwriting. Proper posture and pencil grip are essential early on. We teach children the key abilities: pre-handwriting patterns, sitting, pencil grip and paper tilt. For single letter formation, we follow the RWI program of teaching letter formation alongside the phoneme being taught. We then move onto teaching letters in ‘families’ (letters that are formed in similar ways).
At Burnt Oak, we recognise that handwriting is a fundamental life skill that supports communication, learning, and presentation across the curriculum. We are committed to helping all pupils develop a fluent, legible, and efficient handwriting style that enables them to communicate their ideas effectively and confidently.
Our approach to the teaching and development of handwriting throughout the school and aligns with current research and DfE guidance Writing Framework.
Pupils should be taught handwriting precisely, in a clearly sequenced progression, starting from reception, to support their gradual acquisition of skills. DfE Writing Framework 2025
Handwriting at Burnt Oak aims to:
· Develop clear, legible, and fluent handwriting for all pupils.
· Foster pride in presentation and written work.
· Ensure a consistent approach to handwriting across the school.
· Support pupils in developing the fine motor skills necessary for effective handwriting.
· Enable pupils to write comfortably, efficiently, and at an appropriate speed.
· Provide appropriate support and intervention for pupils experiencing difficulties with handwriting.
The school follows the Ready Steady Write handwriting programme.
Handwriting is taught through:
· Direct, daily and explicit instruction.
· Use of visual patterns and oral patters which supports in embedding the correct letter formation.
· Taught in small, incremental, progressive steps.
· Cumulative, consolidating the teaching.
· This will include regular opportunities to practice and embed the accurate letter formation and joins.
· Opportunities for pupils to practise and apply their handwriting skills across the curriculum.
Teachers will ensure that pupils receive regular feedback on letter formation, size, spacing, orientation and presentation.
Teachers will also ensure that their own handwriting provides a “model of high standards, across the curriculum and not just in handwriting lessons, but particularly when pupils are learning to write.” DfE Writing Framework 2025
Correct Posture and Positioning
Pupils will be taught to:
· Sit comfortably with both feet on the floor where possible.
· Maintain good posture while writing.
· Position paper appropriately.
· Hold writing implements using an effective grip.
· Use their non-writing hand to stabilise the paper.
Staff will model and reinforce correct posture and pencil grip throughout the school.
Support for Left-Handed Pupils
The school recognises that left-handed pupils may require specific guidance to develop comfortable and effective handwriting habits.
Staff will support left-handed pupils by:
· Encouraging an appropriate seating position to avoid elbow clashes with neighbouring pupils.
· Ensuring paper is positioned at an angle that supports natural writing movement.
· Encouraging a comfortable grip and writing position.
· Providing appropriate demonstrations where necessary.
· Monitoring posture and pencil grip to prevent discomfort or inefficient writing habits.
Left-handed pupils will not be expected to adapt their writing style in ways that disadvantage their comfort or progress.
Pupils will have access to suitable writing materials and resources, including:
· Pencils and pens appropriate to their stage of development.
· Handwriting support materials where required.
· Additional resources for intervention and support.
Presentation Expectations
All pupils are expected to:
· Take pride in the presentation of their work.
· Follow agreed school expectations for handwriting and presentation.
· Use the appropriate writing tool as directed by staff.
· Apply taught handwriting skills across all subjects whenever possible.
Assessment and Monitoring
Teachers will assess handwriting regularly through observation of pupils' work and handwriting practice.
Progress will be monitored through:
· Ongoing teacher assessment.
· Summative assessment
· Opportunities for children to edit and improve their own handwriting
· Pupil outcomes across the curriculum.
· Identification of pupils requiring additional support or intervention.
Inclusion and Special Educational Needs
The school is committed to ensuring that all pupils can access handwriting instruction.
Reasonable adjustments will be made for pupils with identified needs, including those with:
· Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND).
· Fine motor difficulties.
· Physical disabilities.
· Medical conditions affecting handwriting.
Where appropriate, alternative methods of recording may be considered in consultation with relevant staff, parents/carers, and external professionals.
Spelling Long Term Progression
We have high expectations in writing and believe that good spelling underpins a child’s enjoyment, confidence and accuracy in writing. When a child lacks confidence and fluency in spelling it can form a barrier when writing across the curriculum. It can also impact on self-confidence and can limit outcomes in writing at the end of KS2. Spelling is an essential skill which allows children to clearly communicate their understanding in writing.
At Burnt Oak we believe that all our children can become fluent, confident and competent spellers. We encourage our pupils to think and write creatively, be adventurous with their use of language and to write with clear purpose and for pleasure. To achieve these aims, it is essential that our pupils develop the knowledge and skills required to spell accurately. We want our pupils to be equipped with both the understanding and a range of strategies for learning spelling, and to be able to apply these strategies effectively when spelling words in their writing.
To ensure this happens, we use the Ready Steady Spell resource. This is a systematic spelling programme that covers all National Curriculum objectives in a cyclical and structured way.
The progression document systematically develops children’s understanding of morphological and phonological spelling knowledge and rules, as appropriate to their stage of learning. It builds on prior knowledge in an incremental and structured manner as pupils move through the school. Children are also taught a range of engaging and interactive strategies to support the recall of spellings and to help embed them into their long-term working memory.

Curriculum Subjects
Burnt Oak Primary School

Burnt Oak Primary School
Assessment
We have a rigorous and shared understanding of all aspects of assessment. Our approach to assessment is at the heart of high quality teaching and learning, inclusive of all abilities, and is used diagnostically for early and accurate identification of pupils' needs, tailored support and intervention.
Our assessment framework for teaching, learning and assessment, recognises and celebrates learning as a journey. The assessment includes short, discrete , qualitative and concrete descriptions of what each pupil is expected to know and be able to do. We focus on making learning and progress visible through daily conversations and interactions with pupils, that actively promote self/peer evaluation and reflection, looking beyond knowledge and understanding to include skills, attitudes and capabilities. We combine formative and summative assessments, using evidence accumulated from day to day teaching and learning, to provide rich evidence over time for our assessment judgements. We ensure assessments are fair, reliable and valid through ongoing internal and external moderation.
Methods for assessment are adapted, to ensure every pupil meets or exceeds expectations, but also so that pupils identified as vulnerable, with SEN or with disabilities are making good progress and are challenged appropriately.
Parents are very welcome in school and we aim to involve them with their children's education as much as possible. Parent consultation meetings take place in the Autumn and Spring term. In addition to this, parents can also arrange appointments to meet with the class teacher and or the Headteacher. At the end of each year, parents receive rich and detailed academic reports on their child's progress, recognising achievements and identifying next steps in their learning.
Our use of assessment aims to inspire the belief that through greater effort, hard work and practice, more can be achieved.
As the main class practitioner, teachers are best placed to know their children’s attainment and progress. Children are regularly assessed as part of normal practice. In every lesson, teachers make snapshot assessments of the work and learning that the children are completing which is used to inform the direction of lessons both in the short and the long term. Regular feedback is given to children so that they are able to build on previous learning and address any errors or misconceptions from previous learning.
From Year 2 – 6 our approach is rooted in the principles of formative assessment and supported by PiXL’s evidence-informed framework. We use PiXL’s DTTR cycle—Diagnose, Therapy, Test, Revisit - to ensure learning gaps are identified and closed effectively:
PiXL’s Language of Assessment categorizes pupils (e.g., Above Expected, Expected, Key Marginal) based on current progress and potential, enabling precise planning and support. This forensic approach aligns with research by Black and Wiliam on formative assessment - using data to inform teaching and improve outcomes.
Additionally, PiXL provides national benchmarking and Implications for Teaching reports, helping us compare performance and refine strategies. This ensures our assessment process is not only rigorous but grounded in theory, promoting mastery and sustained progress.
In Year 1, children are assessed in reading based on the age-appropriate stage they are working at in Read Write Inc. In Maths, they are teacher assessed against National Curriculum objectives

pageCache.pageTitle: Building Foundations | Burnt Oak Primary School
pageCache.text:
Burnt Oak Primary School
🌱 Building Strong Foundations
The best possible start to life at Burnt Oak
The Early Years are where a child's journey at Burnt Oak begins, and we want those first experiences of school to be happy, exciting and full of possibility.
In Nursery and Reception, we create a warm, nurturing and ambitious environment where children feel safe, develop a strong sense of belonging and are encouraged to explore, talk, play, create and discover.
Every child arrives with different experiences, interests and starting points. Our job is to know each child exceptionally well and give them the strong foundations they need to flourish.
Our Early Years provision reflects our whole-school mission: developing the foundations for children's academic, physical and emotional success.
🧱 What Do We Mean by Strong Foundations?
Before children can confidently tackle the increasingly complex learning they will encounter as they move through school, important foundations need to be securely established.
We therefore place particular emphasis on developing:
💬 Communication & LanguageChildren learn to listen, talk, explain, question and communicate confidently. Our classrooms are language-rich environments filled with conversation, stories, songs, rhymes and ambitious vocabulary.
💚 Personal, Social & Emotional DevelopmentChildren learn to understand their emotions, build relationships, develop confidence, manage themselves and become increasingly independent. Our Burnt Oak values of Empathy, Responsibility, Resilience and Respect begin right here.
🏃 Physical DevelopmentChildren develop coordination, strength, balance and control through active learning indoors and outdoors. Fine-motor development also prepares little hands for drawing, mark-making and, eventually, fluent handwriting.
These three prime areas provide vital foundations for children's future learning and development. GOV.UK
📚 Learning to Read, Write and Love Books
We want children to discover that reading opens doors to extraordinary worlds.
Stories, poems, rhymes, songs and high-quality children's books are woven throughout our provision. Children talk about stories, encounter exciting new vocabulary and develop their comprehension through conversation and play.
As children become developmentally ready, they begin systematic phonics through Read Write Inc., learning the sounds and blending skills that allow them to become increasingly confident readers.
Writing begins long before a child writes a sentence. Children develop the physical control, vocabulary, imagination and confidence they need through mark-making, drawing, storytelling and purposeful play.
Our Ready Steady Write approach then provides a carefully structured journey from talk and ideas through to increasingly independent writing.
🔢 Building Brilliant Mathematicians
Early mathematics is about much more than recognising numbers.
🧸 The Power of Play
At Burnt Oak, play is learning.
Our indoor and outdoor environments are carefully designed so that children can explore ideas, practise new knowledge and follow their curiosity.
Adults don't simply supervise play. They observe, question, model vocabulary, introduce new ideas and know when to join children's learning and when to allow children to discover something for themselves.
Through play, children learn to make decisions, solve problems, negotiate, collaborate, persevere and think creatively.
The EYFS describes three important Characteristics of Effective Teaching and Learning:
🔎 Playing and Exploring – investigating, experiencing things and having a go💪 Active Learning – concentrating, persevering and enjoying achievement💡 Creating and Thinking Critically – developing ideas, making connections and finding ways to solve problems. GOV.UK
🌈 Supporting Every Child
Ambition at Burnt Oak is for every child.
We recognise that some children begin their school journey facing additional barriers. This may include children with SEND, children who are disadvantaged, children learning English as an additional language or children who have had different early life experiences.
We identify children's needs early and adapt our teaching and environment so that everyone can participate, belong and succeed.
Our staff work closely with families and, where appropriate, other professionals to provide carefully targeted support.
We believe strongly in keeping up rather than catching up. When we identify a gap in a child's learning, language or development, we respond quickly rather than waiting for that gap to become wider.
🌍 Celebrating Every Language
Children who join us speaking another language already bring valuable knowledge, experiences and language skills with them.
We maintain the same high expectations while providing the additional support children may need to become confident English speakers.
Visuals, modelling, repetition, stories, songs, purposeful conversation and carefully structured adult interactions help children understand and use increasingly rich English while ensuring they remain fully included in the life of their class.
📸 Knowing How Well Our Children Are Doing
Every child develops at their own pace, so our staff get to know children exceptionally well.
Through purposeful observation, conversations, interactions and children's learning, we continually build a picture of what each child knows, understands and can do. This helps us identify strengths, spot any gaps early and decide what each child needs to learn next.
We use this information to:
🔎 identify gaps or additional needs early
⭐ recognise and celebrate children's achievements
📱 Sharing the Journey Through Tapestry
We use Tapestry to give families a window into their child's Early Years experience. Staff share snapshots of significant learning, achievements and special moments so parents and carers can see their child's development in action.
Families can also contribute experiences and achievements from home, helping us build a richer picture of each child and strengthening the partnership between home and school.
Assessment in our Early Years isn't about testing young children. It is about knowing them well, understanding where they are and making sure we know where to take their learning next.
🤝 Working Together with Families
Parents and carers are children's first and most important educators.
Strong relationships between home and school help children thrive. We want families to understand what their child is learning, celebrate their progress and know how they can support learning at home.
We encourage families to talk, play, share stories and read together, because these simple everyday experiences can have a powerful impact on children's development. This partnership with parents is also explicitly emphasised within Development Matters. GOV.UK
🌳 Ready for the Next Adventure
By the end of Reception, our ambition is that children leave the Early Years as happy, confident, curious and increasingly independent learners.
They have developed secure foundations across all seven areas of the EYFS and are ready for the next stage of their learning.
Most importantly, they have learned something that will stay with them far beyond Reception:
Learning is exciting. I can do this. I belong here.
Strong foundations. Happy children. A lifetime of learning.

Burnt Oak Primary School
Curriculum Overview
Our curriculum is formed from a number of different experiences.
Homework will focus on basic skills.
Our Intent
At the Bluebell MAT, we want the best for our children and everything is driven by our shared mission statement:
We all flourish from a wealth of learning experiences that positively impact on academic, physical and emotional success.
Academic Success
Academic success is important for our children who will grow up into a world of increasing technological demands and a diversifying workforce. Academic success boosts self-esteem and impacts positively on behaviours and social interactions within peer groups and with others. Children who are successful academically are more likely to be well-rounded and self-sufficient individuals and will have a wider range of opportunities during their life.
We ensure that children will be academically successful by taking account of an individual’s starting point and helping them to make excellent progress through our curriculum offer. We acknowledge that academic success will look different for every child and will celebrate all progress in order to develop intrinsic self-motivation; to do well for the sake of wanting to do well. We will be driven by our understanding to make choices that will only benefit the children’s academic success.
Physical Success
Physical success is important so that children are able to grow up to be healthy citizens who can make good choices about their lifestyle. Being physically successful helps your brain to work better allowing you to think more clearly, boosts your memory and enhances your concentration and focus. Being physically successful is also important because it has a positive impact on mental health, improving your ability to do everyday activities and adapt and overcome problems or difficulties.
We ensure that children are physically successful through:
PE lessons
Secondary School PE links
Sports clubs
Sports leaders at break
Play/lunch sessions
A range of other activities
Being physically proactive in a lesson
Being ready to learn
Emotional Success
Emotional success is important because it is a key aspect of having a healthy lifestyle. Being self-aware is an important part of being able to work with others successfully and helps us to form meaningful relationships based on an understanding of give and take. Nourishing our social relationships can lead to more success and happiness. Emotional intelligence can help to improve communication and problem solving. It helps to develop empathetic individuals who are able to build relationships based on mutual trust.
We ensure that children are emotionally successful by:
Well established RSHE curriculum
Encouraging independent and collaborative relationships
Appreciating diversity
Maintaining high expectations of behaviour and manners
How we judge the success of our curriculum
We define academic success as:
We define physical success as:
We define emotional success as:
Our curriculum is rooted in a shared set of principles that create a clear and collective understanding of its purpose and intent. These principles promote shared ownership across our school community and extend beyond academic success to embrace children’s development across academic, physical and emotional success. Our curriculum is designed to meet the needs, interests and capabilities of all learners, both now and in the future.
Guided by our core Character Values of Empathy, Respect, Resilience and Responsibility, we aim to develop well-rounded individuals who are not only knowledgeable but also thoughtful, reflective and active citizens. These values underpin our curriculum and are embedded in every aspect of school life, shaping how children learn, interact and flourish.
Our intent is to provide a broad, balanced and ambitious curriculum that inspires curiosity and equips children with the knowledge, skills and character needed to thrive in an ever-changing world. We recognise that success looks different for every child and we are committed to ensuring that all children make excellent progress from their starting points.
Our big idea is to empower every child to understand themselves, others and the world around them, enabling them to make positive contributions to society with confidence, resilience and integrity.
As we have a number of schemes we adopt and adapt, we implement the curriculum in a bespoke way.
At Burnt Oak Primary School, we implement Ready Steady Write as a whole-school writing programme that ensures progression from EYFS to Year 6. Each unit begins with an immersion phase using high-quality, vocabulary-rich texts, followed by structured analysis and planning activities. Daily sentence accuracy tasks reinforce spelling, grammar, and punctuation, while model texts and word banks support pupils in crafting their own writing. Teachers follow a clear sequence—Immerse, Analyse, Plan, Write—aligned with the National Curriculum, and leadership monitors impact through progression documents and CPD, ensuring writing standards remain high across all year groups.
Alongside this, Read Write Inc. is delivered as a systematic phonics and literacy programme to secure early reading and writing success. Daily lessons follow a clear progression of sounds, starting with oral blending and moving through Sets 1–3, supported by handwriting mnemonics and decodable storybooks. Children are regularly assessed and grouped by ability, allowing targeted teaching and interventions. Pupils also develop comprehension and writing skills through activities such as ‘Hold a Sentence’ and ‘Get Writing!’ tasks. Leadership monitors progress using assessment trackers and provides ongoing CPD for staff, ensuring consistent, high-quality implementation across the school.
White Rose Maths is implemented through a mastery approach using carefully sequenced “small steps” to build fluency, reasoning, and problem-solving. Teachers plan from the White Rose schemes of learning and use the CPA (Concrete–Pictorial–Abstract) model to secure deep conceptual understanding. To strengthen retrieval and fluency, daily practice includes PiXL 3-in-3 challenges and TT Rockstars times table rehearsal, ensuring pupils revisit key concepts regularly. These activities are embedded into lessons and linked to ongoing assessment, including end-of-block and termly checks, so teachers can identify gaps and adapt teaching accordingly. Leadership monitors progress through assessment data and curriculum tracking, ensuring consistency and high standards across all year groups.
Jigsaw PSHE & RE is implemented as a whole‑school, spiral curriculum promoting emotional literacy, relationships, health, and spiritual development:
Jigsaw PSHE: Weekly lessons follow six themed “Puzzles” across the year - Being Me in My World, Celebrating Difference, Dreams & Goals, Healthy Me, Relationships, and Changing Me. Each lesson includes a mindfulness 'Calm Me' activity, structured teaching strategies, differentiation for SEND/EAL, and clear progression from EYFS through Year 6. Learning is reinforced via weekly whole-school assemblies and consistent celebration routines, creating shared language and ethos across all classes.

Burnt Oak Primary School
Online Safety
Technology is an important part of children's lives. Children use the internet, games, apps and digital devices to learn, create, play and communicate. These opportunities are hugely valuable, but it is important that children learn how to use technology safely, responsibly and respectfully.
At Burnt Oak Primary School, online safety is an important part of our safeguarding curriculum. We want our children to develop the knowledge, confidence and resilience they need to recognise risks, make sensible choices and know what to do if something worries them online.
Online safety works best when school and families work together. We encourage parents and carers to take an active interest in their child's online life and to have regular, open conversations about the games, apps, websites and devices they use.
Supporting Your Child at Home
Talk regularly about their online world
Ask your child what they enjoy doing online. Rather than only talking about online safety when something has gone wrong, make it part of everyday conversation.
Useful questions might include:
Most importantly, reassure your child that they can always tell a trusted adult if something happens online, even if they have made a mistake themselves.
Know the apps and games your child uses
Take an interest in the games, apps and platforms your child is using. Check their age ratings and age requirements, and explore new games or apps together before allowing your child to use them independently.
Remember that many online games include chat, messaging, friend requests and in-game purchases, even when these are not the main purpose of the game.
Use parental controls and privacy settings
Parental controls can help families manage:
Check privacy and parental-control settings regularly, as apps and devices frequently change.
For younger children in particular, devices should be used where an adult can provide appropriate supervision.
inappropriate or age-restricted content
who can contact your child
in-app purchases
location sharing
screen time
access to particular apps and websites.
Online friends and strangers
Children should understand that people online are not always who they claim to be.
Encourage your child to be cautious about accepting friend requests or communicating privately with people they do not know in real life. They should never arrange to meet somebody they have met online without involving a parent or trusted adult.
Children should also avoid sharing personal information such as their full name, school, address, location, passwords or other private information.
If someone online asks them to keep a conversation secret, requests personal information or images, or asks them to move a conversation onto another app, they should tell a trusted adult.
Be kind and respectful
The Burnt Oak Way applies online too.
Our values of Empathy, Respect, Resilience and Responsibility should guide the way children behave online as well as in school.
Encourage children to stop and think before posting or sending something:
Is it kind? Is it respectful? Is it safe? Would I be happy for a trusted adult to see it?
Online bullying, unkind messages and inappropriate content should never simply be ignored. Children should know how to block, report and tell a trusted adult.
Think before you post
Photos, videos, comments and messages can be copied, shared or screenshotted very quickly. Once something has been shared, it can be difficult to control where it goes next.
Help your child understand their digital footprint and encourage them to think carefully before sharing something about themselves or somebody else.
Children should also ask permission before sharing photographs or videos of other people.
Passwords and account security
Help your child to use strong, unique passwords and remind them that passwords should not be shared with friends.
Where available, use two-step verification (2SV) to provide additional protection for accounts.
Children should also be taught to recognise suspicious messages, links, competitions and offers. If something looks unusual or seems too good to be true, they should check with a trusted adult before clicking.
Not everything online is true
Children are surrounded by online information, videos, influencers, adverts and increasingly AI-generated content.
Help your child develop a questioning approach:
Who created this? Why was it created? Can I trust it? Could it have been changed or generated by AI?
Images, videos and voices can now be convincingly altered or artificially generated. Children should understand that seeing or hearing something online does not automatically make it true.
Artificial Intelligence (AI)
Artificial intelligence is increasingly part of children's digital world. AI tools can provide exciting opportunities for learning and creativity, but children also need to understand their limitations.
Children should be reminded:
Healthy technology habits
Online safety is also about wellbeing. Families may wish to agree expectations around screen time, bedtime, gaming and where devices are kept overnight.
Encourage regular breaks and a healthy balance between online activities and sleep, exercise, hobbies, friendships and family time.
Adults can help by modelling positive digital habits themselves.
If Something Goes Wrong
If your child sees something upsetting, receives an inappropriate message or makes a mistake online, encourage them to stop, block, report and tell.
Try to remain calm and listen. Children are much more likely to ask for help when they know that telling an adult will lead to support rather than immediate punishment or the automatic removal of their device.
If an online incident involves children from Burnt Oak or affects a child's safety, wellbeing or education, please contact the school so that we can provide appropriate support. Where online behaviour affects school, our safeguarding and behaviour procedures may apply.
Further Advice and Support
We recommend the following trusted sources of information for parents and carers:
Below you will also find guidance about some of the apps, games and platforms children may encounter. We strongly encourage parents and carers to check age requirements and safety settings before allowing children to create accounts.
Online safety is not about preventing children from using technology. It is about giving them the knowledge, skills and confidence to enjoy the online world safely and responsibly.

There is also lots of advice you can find on the NSPCC website: https://www.nspcc.org.uk/keeping-children-safe/online-safety/access-to-technology-for-different-ages/
If you have a particular concern or would like to speak about any issue of e-Safety in more detail, please contact Mrs Spratt, Designated Safeguarding Lead.
Useful Links
www.kidsmart.org.uk – Kidsmart is an award-winning Internet safety website for parents and those working with children. It has been developed by the children’s Internet charity, Childnet International, and has excellent information on many of the technologies used by children with guidance on how to stay safe online.
www.thinkuknow.co.uk – Child Exploitation and Online Protection (CEOP) Centre’s website houses a range of information on how to stay safe online. It includes a unique facility that enables parents and young people to make reports of actual or attempted abuse online.
www.childnet-int.org – The Childnet International website gives internet safety advice and links for young people, parents, teachers and other organisations.
www.saferinternet.org.uk – On the UK Safer Internet Centre website, you can find e-safety tips, advice and resources to help children and young people stay safe on the internet.
www.connectsafely.org – This site is built by parents for parents. It offers clearly written guidebooks explaining apps, services and platforms popular with children and teenagers.
www.betterinternetforkids.eu – A site promoting safe digital habits for children throughout Europe. It has blog posts trending internet topics and even has a hotline where families can receive support and report anything suspicious online.

Burnt Oak Primary School
Amazing Play, Every Day, for Every Child 🌳
At Burnt Oak, we believe that play matters.
We are proud to be on our journey towards becoming an OPAL school, transforming our playtimes so that every child has exciting, creative and meaningful opportunities to play every day.
OPAL (Outdoor Play and Learning) is a nationally recognised, mentor-supported school improvement programme which helps schools develop high-quality, inclusive and sustainable play.
Why is play so important?
Children spend around 20% of their time at primary school playing. Across their primary years, that is equivalent to approximately 1.4 years of school!
We want that time to be every bit as valuable as the time children spend in the classroom.
Through great play, children have opportunities to:
🧠 imagine, create and problem-solve
💚 develop friendships and social skills
💪 be active and develop physically
🌱 build resilience, confidence and independence
🤝 cooperate, negotiate and resolve problems
😊 support their emotional wellbeing
This fits perfectly with our Burnt Oak mission of helping every child flourish and achieve academic, physical and emotional success.
What does OPAL look like at Burnt Oak?
OPAL is about giving children choice, freedom, creativity and challenge within a carefully managed environment.
Over our OPAL journey, children will have access to a much richer range of play experiences. This may include:
🛞 Loose PartsTyres, crates, tubes, ropes, fabric and other open-ended resources that can become almost anything in a child's imagination.
🏗️ Building & CreatingOpportunities to design, construct, invent and work together.
🌿 Exploring OutdoorsMaking greater use of our school grounds throughout the year and experiencing nature, mud, water and the changing seasons.
🎭 Imaginative PlaySpaces and resources that encourage role play, performance, creativity and storytelling.
🏃 Active & Challenging PlayRunning, climbing, balancing, moving and taking appropriate risks in a managed environment.
💚 Something for EveryoneDifferent children enjoy different types of play. Our aim is to create opportunities where every child can belong, participate and flourish.
A Little More Freedom... and Sometimes a Little More Mud! 🌧️
Great outdoor play means children will use more of our grounds, in more ways, throughout more of the year.
That means children may sometimes come home a little muddier than they used to!
It also means they are learning to assess appropriate risks, solve problems, make decisions, manage relationships and become increasingly independent.
Our approach is carefully planned and managed, balancing children's need for challenge and adventure with their safety and wellbeing.
The Impact of Great Play
Schools taking part in OPAL report significant benefits including happier children, improved behaviour, increased physical activity, stronger social and emotional development and children returning to lessons more settled and ready to learn.
For us, OPAL is much more than improving lunchtime.
It is about giving our children a richer childhood.
🧰 Can You Help Our OPAL Journey?
As our play provision develops, we may ask families and our wider community to donate loose parts and resources that can be safely reused for play.
You might be surprised by what makes a brilliant play resource: crates, tyres, fabric, guttering, pots, pans, tubes and other everyday objects can unlock extraordinary creativity.
Keep an eye on our newsletters for our OPAL donation requests and updates as our playground continues to grow and change.
🌳 Amazing play. Every day. Every child.
Play • Explore • Create • Challenge • Flourish
🌿 Find Out More About OPAL
Want to discover more about why great play matters?
OPAL has worked with thousands of schools to transform playtimes and create happier, healthier and more active childhoods. Research and evidence from the programme highlights improvements in wellbeing, behaviour, inclusion, physical activity, social development and children's ability to recognise and manage risk.
